c1: The join is clean: "In the end that press got us more users" completes the cut at "In ". The continuation is about 108 words, which is within range, and it does not repeat the excerpt. This criterion is essentially met.

c2: The answer touches the mechanism with "press got us more users". It then shifts to an unsupported claim that the PR firm "paid the reporters to write the stories up". That contradicts the excerpt's "reporters liked us", which implies the coverage was genuine. It never explains why press worked or how it converted users. The ending "The web has changed since then... very little out of pocket expense" restates the excerpt's premise rather than developing it.

c3: The voice is mostly informal and economical. The shift to second person ("You paid the firm", "You just had to have the nerve") weakens the first-person plural memoir voice. The bribery claim ("so obviously rigged", "everyone was doing the same thing") is fabricated, unsupported content about real events. The closing line is mildly uplifting and generic: "great deal of attention for very little".
